title: Index Sort
statement: You are given an integer array nums of size n containing a permutation of integers from 1 to n. Your goal is to sort the array in ascending order. You must choose a fixed integer k (1 <= k <= n). Once k is chosen, you can swap any two indices i and j as long as neither i nor j equals k. Return the total number of distinct values of k for which it is possible to sort the array into ascending order.

examples.explanation: The array is already sorted. Every index k satisfies nums[k-1] == k, so every value of k is valid.
Only k = 3 works (nums[2] = 3). For k = 1 or k = 2, misplaced elements at index k cannot be moved because swaps involving k are forbidden.
No index k has nums[k-1] == k, so no value of k allows the array to be sorted.

constraints: nums is a permutation of integers from 1 to n.
hints: Hint 1: Index k is forbidden from participating in any swaps, so nums[k-1] can never move.
Hint 2: For the final array to be sorted, position k must end up with value k.
Hint 3: Since nums[k-1] cannot move, k is valid if and only if nums[k-1] == k.
discussion: Count how many indices i (0-based) satisfy nums[i] == i + 1.
